title: Probit models for discrete choice data
text: RprobitB function fit() estimates following model variants: binary, multinomial, ordered, ranked responses, cross-sectional panel data, correlated uncorrelated normal log-normal random effects, latent classes fixed, sparse finite, Dirichlet-process based number components. Modeling preference heterogeneity covers random coefficients six mixing distributions latent classes fixed, sparse finite, Dirichlet-process based number components. Posterior prediction covers predictions population individual deciders, scenarios new data, residuals, marginal effects. Bayesian model evaluation covers model comparison via WAIC, PSIS-LOO, Bayes factors. Posterior draws stored posterior format. Chains can run parallel future plan. examples use data sets mlogit, AER, MASS, choicedata packages, introduced vignettes.
